paraphrase: Which sūtras are of definitive meaning (nītārtha) and which of provisional meaning (neyārtha)? Those that teach the conventional — the establishment of the path, of self, being, soul, person, agent — are provisional; those that teach emptiness, the signless, the wishless, the unconditioned, the unborn, no self, no being, no soul, no person, no owner, are definitive.

paraphrase: The four reliances: rely on the meaning, not the letter; on the dharma, not the person; on gnosis (jñāna), not consciousness (vijñāna); on sūtras of definitive meaning, not provisional meaning.
